map.3月龄幼犬的如厕时间窗: Toilet time window for a 3-month-old puppy
map.按“月龄+1小时”规则，3月龄幼犬憋尿上限 ≈ 3+1 = 4 小时（成年犬上限: Under the rule of age in months + 1 hour, a 3-month-old puppy can hold for about 3 + 1 = 4 hours (adult dogs are capped at 8 hours; cats use age in months + 2 hours, capped at 10 hours). Key elimination windows: within about 5 minutes after waking, 15–30 minutes after drinking or eating, and within about 10 minutes after play. So if a puppy has just woken up and drank 15 minutes ago, guide it to the spot immediately; 4 hours is the maximum holding time, and exceeding it risks indoor accidents.
map.幼犬和成犬的憋尿能力差多少？: How much does bladder capacity differ between puppies and adults?
map.幼犬约为“月龄+1小时”（3月龄≈4h、5月龄≈6h），成年犬统一按 6–8 小: Puppies roughly follow age in months + 1 hour (3 months ≈ 4 h, 5 months ≈ 6 h); adult dogs are uniformly counted as 6–8 hours; cats tolerate slightly longer (age in months + 2 hours, capped at 10 hours). The younger the animal, the shorter the window and the more often it needs to be taken out.

map.3 月龄幼犬：最长憋尿参考约 4 小时（教学示例，非个体上限）。排尿参考：饮水后: 3-month puppy: max hold reference ~4 h (teaching example, not an individual limit). Urine reference 15–30 min after drinking; stool reference ~30–120 min after eating; elimination is common after waking or play. Drinking 15 min ago only means the example window has started—watch for signals; it does not guarantee elimination. After 3 logged urine times (e.g. 20/25/30, average 25 min), use the local average; a single abnormal event or inability to urinate needs a vet.
map.“月龄+1小时”和猫“月龄+2小时”只是教学参考，不是膀胱容量或个体上限；实际受: “Age months + 1 hour” for dogs and “+2 hours” for cats are teaching references, not bladder capacity or individual limits; intake, activity, environment and health all matter. Calibrate with local records and consult a vet for abnormal signs.
